Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১) What is the probability of getting a sum 9 from two throws of a dice?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: What is the probability of getting a sum 9 from two throws of a dice?

Solution:
Total events = 6 × 6 = 36
Set of expected events = {(3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3)}

∴ probability of getting a sum 9 from two throws of a dice = 4/36 = 1/9

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৭) Two cards are drawn together from a pack of 52 cards. The probability that one is a diamond and one is a heart, is?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two cards are drawn together from a pack of 52 cards. The probability that one is a diamond and one is a heart, is?

Solution:
Two cards can be drawn together from a standard deck in = 52C2 = 1326 ways.

One diamond can be drawn in = 13C1 ways
and a heart too can be drawn in = 13C1 ways.

Therefore, the number of ways that a diamond and a heart can be drawn = 13C1 × 13C1
= 13 × 13
= 169

Therefore, the required probability = 169/1326
= 13/102

Bank-Math-Master\t.question:
৯) What is the mean of the range, mode and median of the data given below?
4, 15, 3, 4, 4, 8, 9, 3, 10, 2, 9, 5, 11, 19, 6
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: What is the mean of the range, mode and median of the data given below?
4, 15, 3, 4, 4, 8, 9, 3, 10, 2, 9, 5, 11, 19, 6

Solution:
Arranging the given data in ascending order 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 10, 11, 15, 19
Here,
Most frequent data is 4
so Mode = 4

Total terms in the given data, (n) = 15 (It is odd)
Median = {(n + 1)/2}(th) term
= {(15 + 1)/2}(th) term
= (8)th term
= 6

Now, Range = Maximum value - Minimum value = 19 - 2 = 17

Mean of Range, Mode and median = (Range + Mode + Median)/3
= (17 + 4 + 6)/3
= 27/3
= 9

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১০) Three unbiased coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at most two heads?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Three unbiased coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at most two heads?

Solution:
Getting at most Two heads means 0 to 2 but not more than 2.

Here S = {TTT, TTH, THT, HTT, ΤΗΗ, ΗΤΗ, HHT, HHH}

Let E = event of getting at most two heads
Then E = {TTT, TTH, THT, HTT, THH, HTH, HHT}

∴ P(E) = n(E)/n(S) = 7/8

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৪) If x<sup>2</sup> − 8x +15 < 0 then solve the inequality-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: If x2 − 8x +15 < 0 then solve the inequality-

Solution:
Given,
x2 − 8x +15 < 0
⇒ x2 - 3x - 5x + 15 < 0
⇒ x(x - 3) - 5(x - 3) < 0
⇒ (x - 3)(x - 5) < 0

The inequality will be true if x - 3 > 0 and x - 5 < 0 .
x - 3 > 0
or, x > 3

x - 5 < 0
or, x < 5
The inequality will be true if 3 < x < 5

∴ The solution of the inequality is 3 < x < 5

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৫) A committee of 5 members is to be formed by selecting out of 6 men and 7 women. What is the probability that the committee has exactly 2 men and 3 women?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A committee of 5 members is to be formed by selecting out of 6 men and 7 women. What is the probability that the committee has exactly 2 men and 3 women?

Solution:
Total member = 3 + 2 = 5

2 men can be selected out of 6 men = 6C2 ways
3 women can be selected out of 7 women in = 7C3 ways
Required number of ways = 6C2 × 7C3 = 15 × 35 = 525

The total number of ways to make committee with all members = 13C5 = 1287

∴ The probability that the committee has exactly 2 men and 3 women = 525/1287
= 175/429

Solution:

⇒ (x − 6)(x − 12) ≥ 0

x - 6 ≤ 0
⇒ x ≤ 6

x - 12 ≥ 0
⇒ x ≥ 12
The inequality will be true if x ≤ 6 or x ≥ 12

∴ The solution of the inequality is x ≤ 6 or x ≥ 12
